propositions: The 'undecomposed' hard-override axis fires only 0.107% (plan-v3) and 0.153% (plan-v4) of verified findings, two orders of magnitude below other severity axes, but the cited G5 deterministic suppressor (explanation for low rate) never actually fired across 2,000 reviews.

The G5 deterministic suppressor inert state contradicts the stated rationale: 90%+ of reviewed tickets are childless so the suppressor is inapplicable, and the coverage key 'g5_undecomposed_vetoed' is absent from every sidecar (zero vetos).

The hard-override floor (0.85) gates on non-none grade, causing 'low' grade findings to produce the same impact as 'high', making 25 of 29 fires dependent solely on the floor for their block status, exactly paralleling the miscalibration already fixed for ac_unverifiable and divergent_implementation axes.

Inverse-population analysis found 33 plan-v3 and 17 plan-v4 findings whose text matches the undecomposed regex but scored none; sampling shows these are code-decomposition false positives unrelated to plan decomposition, not a missed dark class of flat-plan defects.
The axis text in reviewer prompts cites the inert G5 suppressor as justification for conservative grading, factually misleading given zero measured suppression and 90%+ inapplicability.
